bottom_line: In apparently healthy men and women with LDL cholesterol <130 mg per deciliter and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ≥2.0 mg per liter, rosuvastatin 20 mg daily vs placebo reduced the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46 to 0.69).
implications: These data support that, in this enrolled population and during the observed follow-up, rosuvastatin 20 mg daily reduced the rate of the combined primary end point (0.77 vs 1.36 per 100 person-years; hazard ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.69) and was associated with more physician-reported diabetes (270 vs 216 reports). Because the trial was stopped early after a median follow-up of 1.9 years, this document notes uncertainty about longer-term adverse events.

major_points.text: Participants were apparently healthy with LDL cholesterol <130 mg/dl and hsCRP ≥2.0 mg/L.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 17,802 apparently healthy men and women with low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels of 2.0 mg per liter or higher

major_points.text: Intervention was rosuvastatin 20 mg daily compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: Eligible subjects were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either rosuvastatin, 20 mg daily, or matching placebo.

major_points.text: Primary end point was a first major cardiovascular event (MI, stroke, unstable angina hospitalization, arterial revascularization, or confirmed cardiovascular death).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was the occurrence of a first major cardiovascular event, defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, an arterial revascularization procedure, or confirmed death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early after the first prespecified efficacy evaluation crossed the stopping boundary; median follow-up 1.9 years.
major_points.quote: The trial was stopped after a median follow-up of 1.9 years (maximum, 5.0).

major_points.text: Rosuvastatin reduced the primary end point versus placebo.
major_points.quote: The rates of the primary end point were 0.77 and 1.36 per 100 person-years of follow-up in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, respectively (hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69; P<0.00001)
